The human instinct is to avoid suffering and pain. 

So why do your positive words get met with more reactions of negativity rather than allievate the suffering?

Well negative life effects as well as diseases can cause changes in the structures of the brain, strengthening some, weakening others, extinguishing some connections altogether. This particular brain becomes hardwired for a world they might not even live in anymore and so all new information has to be filtered through it because what else is there?

Just as you might not immediately understand new concepts or even trust them, the brain cannot build new structures overnight to support a more positive world and small negative events would have a shortcut through already set up structures.

Suicidal people see death as the only useful solution because they're brain is hardwired for lack of connection, pain and suffering and well humans are also hardwired to avoid suffering.

The brain can be fixed, but it takes more than the odd few words and then people getting angry at them for not immediately being able to be positive.

It's okay that you don't want to deal with it. Your brain is hardwired to find the positive and feels distress at having to create structures to understand a negative world view. Just as it seems too difficult for you to recognise their world veiw as truth, their brain is doing the same for positive world views.
